messages.content: I'm working with a chatbot to provide accurate responses based on user queries. For instance, if someone is asking for the bank's routing number, how can I identify that the intent is to get banking information? Also, what should I do if the query is about activating a new bank card?

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the response based on user intent. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request will be sent. Format should be a valid URL string, such as 'https://example.com/resource'.

intent.description: The intent of the user, selected from a predefined list of intents.

probability.description: The probability of the provided intent being the correct one. Value should be between 0.0 and 1.0, where 0.0 indicates least confidence and 1.0 indicates highest confidence. This is a float type value.

message.content:
### 1. Identifying the Intent | Intent | Typical Keywords / Phrases | Example User Query | |--------|---------------------------|--------------------| | **Banking Information** | “routing number”, “account number”, “IBAN”, “SWIFT code”, “bank details” | “What’s the bank’s routing number?” | | **Card Activation** | “activate card”, “new card activation”, “card activation steps”, “activate my new card” | “How do I activate my new bank card?” | | **Account Balance** | “balance”, “current balance”, “how much do I have” | “Show me my account balance.” | | **Transaction History** | “transactions”, “recent activity”, “statement”, “payment history” | “Give me my last 10 transactions.” | | **Support / Troubleshooting** | “problem”, “issue”, “error”, “help”, “cannot login” | “I can’t log into my account.” | | **Feedback / Complaints** | “feedback”, “complaint”, “suggestion”, “report” | “I’d like to give feedback about the app.” | | **General Inquiry** | “what”, “how”, “why”, “information”, “details” | “What are your business hours?” | #### How to Build the Classifier 1. **Collect Sample Queries** Gather a diverse set of user messages for each intent. Include variations in phrasing, typos, and slang. 2. **Choose a Method** * **Rule‑Based / Keyword Matching** – Fast, easy to implement. Use a lookup table of keywords → intent. * **Machine Learning** – Train a text classifier (e.g., logistic regression, SVM, or a transformer model). Requires labeled data but scales better. 3. **Preprocess Text** * Lowercase, remove punctuation. * Tokenize, optionally lemmatize or stem. * Remove stop‑words if using ML. 4. **Feature Extraction** * **Keyword Matching** – Count occurrences of intent keywords. * **ML** – Convert tokens to vectors (TF‑IDF, word embeddings, or BERT embeddings). 5. **Train / Tune** * Split data into training/validation sets. * Optimize hyperparameters (e.g., regularization strength, learning rate). * Evaluate using precision/recall/F1 per intent. 6. **Deploy** * Wrap the classifier in an API endpoint. * Log predictions and confidence scores for monitoring. 7. **Iterate** * Continuously collect new queries, label them, and retrain. * Add new intents or refine keyword lists as needed. --- ### 2. Handling a “New Card Activation” Query When the intent is identified as **Card Activation**, follow these steps to ensure a smooth, secure, and compliant experience: | Step | Action | Why It Matters | |------|--------|----------------| | **1. Verify Identity** | • Ask for the user’s full name, last 4 digits of SSN, or a one‑time password (OTP) sent to their registered phone/email.
• If the user is already authenticated in the session, confirm that the session belongs to the same person. | Prevents fraud and ensures the user is who they claim to be. | | **2. Confirm Card Details** | • Prompt the user to enter the last 4 digits of the new card or the card’s serial number.
• Optionally ask for the card’s expiration date. | Helps match the card to the user’s account. | | **3. Provide Activation Instructions** | • Offer two activation methods:
 a. **Online Activation** – “Enter your card number and the OTP you received.”
 b. **Phone Activation** – “Call our 24/7 support line at 1‑800‑XXX‑XXXX.”
• Explain any required PIN or security questions. | Gives the user flexibility and clear guidance. | | **4. Guide Through the Process** | • If online: “Enter the OTP you received via SMS.”
• If phone: “Speak with a representative and provide the card number and OTP.” | Keeps the user engaged and reduces confusion. | | **5. Confirm Success** | • Once activated, display a confirmation message: “Your card has been successfully activated.”
• Optionally send a push notification or email. | Provides closure and reassurance. | | **6. Offer Additional Help** | • Ask if the user needs help with setting up a PIN, adding the card to a mobile wallet, or any other related tasks.
• Provide links to FAQs or a live chat option. | Enhances user satisfaction and reduces repeat inquiries. | | **7. Log & Monitor** | • Record the activation event, timestamps, and any errors.
• Monitor for unusual patterns (e.g., many failed activations). | Supports compliance, audit trails, and fraud detection. | #### Sample Dialogue Flow ``` User: How do I activate my new bank card? Bot: Great! Let’s get started. First, could you confirm your full name as it appears on your account? User: John Doe Bot: Thanks, John. Please enter the last 4 digits of your new card. User: 1234 Bot: Got it. We’ve sent an OTP to the phone number on file. Please enter the 6‑digit code. User: 567890 Bot: Your card has been successfully activated! Would you like to set up a PIN or add this card to Apple Pay/Google Pay? User: No, thanks. Bot: You’re all set! If you need anything else, just let me know. ``` --- ### 3. Quick Checklist for Implementation - [ ] **Intent List** – Maintain a master list of intents and associated keywords. - [ ] **Confidence Threshold** – Set a minimum confidence (e.g., 0.7) before acting on an intent. - [ ] **Fallback Strategy** – If confidence is low, ask clarifying questions or route to human support. - [ ] **Security** – Ensure all personal data is handled per PCI‑DSS and GDPR requirements. - [ ] **Testing** – Simulate edge cases (misspellings, ambiguous queries) to validate robustness. - [ ] **Analytics** – Track intent distribution, success rates, and time to resolution. --- ### 4. Next Steps 1. **Build or Update Your Intent Classifier** – Use the guidelines above to create a reliable model. 2. **Integrate the Activation Flow** – Embed the activation logic into your chatbot platform. 3. **Run Pilot Tests** – Deploy to a small user group, collect feedback, and iterate. 4. **Scale** – Roll out to all users once confidence and accuracy metrics meet your SLA targets. Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper dives into any of these areas—whether it’s the technical details of the classifier, the exact wording for the activation prompts, or compliance considerations.
